svg.title: Making the Seller the Bank, by the Percentages
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-07-seller-finance-vs-bank-entry; chapter number: 4; title: Making the Seller the Bank, by the Percentages; subtitle: Creative entry cost against bank down payments and seller-note rates; caption: Pace Morby's average 8% entry compares with the 30-35% down a bank requires, while Key & Capital models seller notes at 6-9%.; assumptions note: Buckets are percentages reported by different practitioners and are shown side by side, not summed.; note: Sources: Pace Morby (_M0q3Da-vxU), Key & Capital (dzuLMB2Szxc), Flipping Mastery TV (-E2cCPmM_Q0).; chart type: stacked_comparison; total range: 8% creative entry vs 30-35% bank down payment (percent of price); buckets: label: Pace Morby Average All-In Entry; low: 8; high: 8; notes: Down payment plus closing costs, about 8%.; label: Bank Down Payment Requirement; low: 30; high: 35; notes: $80-100K on a $300K house, per Pace Morby.; label: Key & Capital Seller-Note Rates; low: 6; high: 9; notes: Modeled with 5-7 year balloons; a 0% seller note is not clever.; label: Real Estate Owned Free and Clear; low: 30; high: 30; notes: Pace's sizing of the seller-finance target pool.
